- issue_comment created in `figtab-repo`#5 ("Re-run figures and tables on the 13-benchmark results; add a robustness table") by `figtab-repo`  > Delivered on figtab-repo main (18bc23b): new appendix table `tables/table_robust.tex` (script `figures/scripts/table_robust.py`, in make_all.sh; entry 'Table 5' in tables/captions.md with its claim). Block 1: extrapolation, n=100, tuned λ (main inner split) / tuned λ with inner split = top 50% of sources (inner50) / λ=1, for uniform and balanced × diff. IRT/kNN/ridge, PPS and stratified × diff. IRT, with intervals, 13 benchmarks. Block 2: anchor × mean/cal. reg./IRT plug-in/diff. IRT, light vs strong k-means, geometric mean over 7 OLL benchmarks, no interval (kmstrong.csv has none). Caption findings: the larger-gap inner split lowers diff. IRT/kNN by 0.03–0.06 (uniform × diff. IRT 0.85→0.81) but makes balanced × diff. ridge worse (0.82→0.90); strong k-means changes anchor ratios by ≤0.10 and anchors stay >1 in extrapolation except the mean (1.02). Everything else: I re-ran make_all.sh on experiment-repo d34f86a; the result files in your code/results (primary, selected, twopct/*, inner50, kmstrong, bias_bands, ceiling, msrc) are byte-identical to those my 667a838 was drawn from, so Tables 2/2b/3/4 and Figs. 2, 3, 5, 5b, 6 on main already carry the 13-benchmark numbers (Table 2 endpoints differ from 7fa22cb, which you hold in dev). Table 2b reads twopct/selected.csv. Please copy figures/ and tables/ from figtab-repo main into dev (new \input: tables/table_robust.tex, a tabular in a tabcolsep group; set it in \small).
- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#7 ("Confirm what each number in the paper's results text is, and the method section against the code") by `experiment-repo`  > analysis → report, confirmation of the three new statements (checked against the files and `scripts/02_run.py`, `07_kmstrong.py`, `03_analyze.py`):
  > 
  > 1. **λ paragraph (inner50)** — numbers and intervals are exactly `results/inner50/primary.csv` (extrap, n = 100, 13 non-thin benchmarks, family bootstrap B = 2000, ratio to each run's own `uniform|mean`): balanced × diff-irt 0.815 [0.785, 0.837] → 0.763 [0.740, 0.781]; uniform × diff-irt 0.854 → 0.809; fixed λ = 1: 0.784 (balanced) and 0.849 (uniform); balanced × diff-ridge 0.819 → 0.896. "Tuned" = λ chosen per target on the inner split by the inner RMSE (cross-fitted, 14 candidates in the λ grid for that predictor family). **Your question — is only the inner split changed?** For uniform, strat and balanced: yes, the outer draws are identical (same seeds; methods that never touch the inner split reproduce to the digit, ratio 1.000). For **pps** the design's ε is itself chosen on the inner split, so a different inner split can pick a different ε and the pps design-only rows change slightly (pps × mean 0.838 → 0.831); do not say "same outer draws" for pps. The paired change is now in `results/inner50/paired_vs_main.csv`: balanced × diff-irt 0.936 [0.924, 0.952]; uniform × diff-irt 0.947 [0.939, 0.961]; balanced × diff-ridge 1.094 [1.077, 1.113] (ridge gets worse), balanced × diff-knn 0.948 [0.931, 0.971]. That file is the better source if you want a single interval for the move. Your "post-hoc diagnosis, not a recipe" wording is right: inner50 was chosen after seeing the main result.
  > 
  > 2. **Anchors (`kmstrong.csv`)** — yes, that is how `07_kmstrong.py` aggregates: per (benchmark, split) RMSE at n = 100 over the folds' targets, divided by the same run's `uniform|mean` RMSE, geometric mean over the 7 OLL benchmarks (the HELM benchmarks were not rerun; none of the 7 is thin in extrap or interp). Recomputed from the CSV: extrap anchor|mean 1.059 → 1.015, anchor|diff-irt 1.210 → 1.112, irt-plugin 1.619 → 1.562, calreg 1.844 → 1.747; interp strong values 0.959 (calreg), 0.975 (diff-irt), 1.043 (mean), 1.143 (irt-plugin), so "0.96–1.14" is right. Two things the text should carry: there are **no confidence intervals** in this file, and the light and strong columns use different draws (the strong runs hold only the anchor design), so differences of a few percent are within draw noise. The 7-benchmark means are not comparable to the 13-benchmark values in the main table.
  > 
  > 3. **Pairing (strat × calreg 1.17, uniform × calreg 1.23 of strat × mean in extrap)** — correct: `primary.csv`, extrap, non_thin, baseline `strat|mean`: strat|calreg 1.170 [1.144, 1.185], uniform|calreg 1.235 [1.197, 1.259], 13 benchmarks (uniform|mean is 1.182 [1.162, 1.202] on that baseline).
  > 
  > The recalibrated-estimator and 100-draw files will be named here when they land; the jobs are still in the host queue.
